solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Seem joyful, with a little excited sound, getting some food

parts.note: to bubble is to be lively and full of joy
and means together with
a squeak is a short high-pitched cry of excitement

explanation.surface: Someone squeals with delight on being handed something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubble and squeak is a British dish of fried leftover cabbage and potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British fry-up of leftover vegetables is an example of food.

clue.text: Fool — naked in this, and having this?

parts.note: naked is 'in the buff', so the word that completes the phrase
naked is also having nothing on: O for nothing, then ON

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a clown's costume, or lack of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe being naked: 'in the buff', and having O (nothing) on. The pieces join as BUFF, O, ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A clownish person who behaves ridiculously is a synonym of fool.

clue.text: Make love? Predict embracing in this way

indicators.note: embracing means the forecast word holds the other piece within its arms

parts.note: to bet that something will happen is to predict it
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A forecaster tells a couple how to make love.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Make love' means cause to be infatuated, not the physical act.
explanation.definitionFit: To infatuate someone is to make them fall in love, the verb's main sense.

clue.text: Fail to get up to island to catch first sight of wind hover

parts.note: to lie in is to stay in bed rather than get up

indicators.note: the first sight of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames

explanation.surface: Someone oversleeps instead of travelling to an island to watch the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' is link wording: the island piece follows the first letter of 'wind'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurk in ambush is to hover nearby, waiting for a chance to strike.

clue.text: A throw of the dice coming up: all revolves around this

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a six is a top throw of a die

explanation.surface: A dice game where everything turns on a lucky roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating body spins about a central line, so the line is what all turns around.

clue.text: Constable in Irish town crosses quaking bog

indicators.note: crosses means the town name lies across the other piece, holding it

parts.note: Derry is a city in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: quaking means the letters shake into a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman in an Irish town wades across trembling marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: The constable is the bumbling watchman in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic watchman is a famous fictional constable, malapropisms and all.

clue.text: Question given to a sailor: who won the cup in 2010?

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A quiz question put to a sailor about a sports winner.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2010 this Gulf state won the vote to host the 2022 World Cup, not a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf emirate was awarded the football World Cup hosting rights by FIFA in 2010.

clue.text: Succeeded in designing emoticon for the publication

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
designing means the letters are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: S is short for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone gets ahead by drawing a smiley face for a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'emoticon' is ECONOMIT, with S placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Economist is a well-known weekly British news magazine, so it is the publication.

clue.text: Sound money only divided region

indicators.note: sound means the pieces are spoken and the result is written as heard

parts.note: cash is money and mere means only, together a wool fabric's name

explanation.surface: A sound economy is all about money in a region split apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'solid', as in sound money, but signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan territory is split between India, Pakistan and China, so a divided region.

clue.text: Becoming bitter, call on clown

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means the call word comes after the clown

parts.note: Feste is the clown in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A sulking person rings up a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that rankles and grows more resentful over time is said to be rotting inside.

clue.text: Love having children about, being gentle Dickensian

indicators.note: about means the children word goes around the other piece

parts.note: tots are small children
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A kindly Victorian figure is surrounded by loving children.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toots is the good-natured, simple character in Dickens's Dombey and Son.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Toots in Dombey and Son is a kindly character created by the Victorian novelist.

clue.text: Revealing orientation of journey

definitions.meaning: making public someone's sexuality, often against their will

explanation.surface: A trip that reveals which way someone is facing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a public exposure of someone's sexuality and an excursion.

clue.text: Next in line to Gents, male that has been there a long time — priceless?

definitions.text: that has been there a long time — priceless?

parts.note: an heir is next in line to inherit
the Gents is a men's toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: An ancient, valuable men's lavatory next in the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A family treasure handed down through generations is old and may be beyond price.

clue.text: Cardinal, as he was after baptism?

definitions.meaning: John Henry, the Victorian churchman who became a cardinal and saint
baptism makes a person spiritually reborn, a fresh person

explanation.surface: A churchman reborn by baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal John Henry Newman converted to Catholicism; baptism makes one a reborn person.

clue.text: Administrators knock what fits into partition

indicators.note: fits into means the first pieces go inside the partition word

parts.note: a wall is a partition
to knock is to hit
eh? is a request to repeat, like what?

explanation.surface: Someone bangs on a dividing wall to see what fits.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries, standing for the civil service.
explanation.definitionFit: The street name stands by metonymy for the British civil service, the government's administrators.

clue.text: Leisure worker, one with throat condition worsening?

definitions.meaning: a casino employee who runs a gaming table
comparative of croupy, more afflicted with croup

explanation.surface: A worker whose sore throat is getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino table attendant works in the leisure industry; jokingly, also 'more croupy'.

clue.text: I cut and run, confusing big number — that's rash

indicators.note: confusing means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
an aria is a big solo number in opera

explanation.surface: Someone flees after muddling a large figure, a hasty act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' turns I, CUT and R into URTIC; 'big number' is a song, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettle rash, or hives, is an itchy skin rash, the medical name's everyday sense.

clue.text: Into container, airmen fit endless fuel

indicators.note: into means the airmen and trimmed word go inside the container

parts.note: a pan is a container
the RAF is the Royal Air Force

indicators.note: endless means the word fit loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Airmen squeeze fuel into a can, without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin, or kerosene, is a fuel burned in lamps, heaters and jet engines.

clue.text: I put in hasty article, ferociously satirical

indicators.note: put in means the I goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: swift means quick, hasty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer hastily adds a savage satirical piece to the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal, savage satires.
explanation.definitionFit: Derived from Jonathan Swift, the term describes biting, savage satire in his manner.

clue.text: Live together with journalist, surrounded by drink

indicators.note: surrounded by means the journalist sits inside the drink word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: Moving in with a reporter who is always drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrasal verb means to cohabit with a lover without marrying.

clue.text: Standing figure, 21

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a figure
21 across is American, abbreviated US

explanation.surface: A standing statue, American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing figure' reads as a statue, but 'Standing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's standing is their rank or position in society.

clue.text: Pathetic, involving church in devilish practices

indicators.note: involving means the pathetic word wraps around the church

parts.note: sorry means pitiful, pathetic
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pitiful church mixed up in satanic rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Black magic invoking evil spirits is a set of devilish practices.

clue.text: Last word about one of the Costas: it's continental

indicators.note: about means the last word goes around the other piece

parts.note: amen is the final word of a prayer
Costa Rica, with Rica the second part of its name

explanation.surface: A final word on a Spanish holiday coast being continental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Costas' suggests Spain's resort coasts, but the one meant is Costa Rica.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to one of the two continents of the Americas makes something continental.

clue.text: Lazed around in wind regularly light

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word

parts.note: to light the way is to guide, past tense led

explanation.surface: Lounging about in the breeze with a little lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Lounging about doing nothing is to have wasted time lazily.

clue.text: Duck's back holding firm as tail's docked

indicators.note: holding means the trimmed word contains the firm
a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A duck's back stays strong even with its tail clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Not entirely forgotten, noble emperor

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, a run within them

explanation.surface: A noble emperor who is half remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese title for the emperor, a sovereign of a heavenly line.

clue.text: Decided with husband to have third child

parts.note: set means fixed or decided

explanation.surface: A couple make up their minds to have a third baby.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve's third son, born after Cain and Abel.

clue.text: Bit of fun, turning over a village

indicators.note: over means the reversed word goes over and around the a
turning means the fun word is read backwards

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun

explanation.surface: A prank overturning a whole village.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern Africa this is a traditional enclosed village of huts.

clue.text: Having no charge, managed say to get back without using battery

parts.note: free means costing nothing
ran means managed, as a business

indicators.note: to get back means the word for say is turned round

parts.note: eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A battery runs free of charge, then is managed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battery' looks electrical but means battery farming of hens.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens kept outdoors rather than in battery cages are raised without that system.

clue.text: Exaggerated distress as phony delegation is turfed out

indicators.note: turfed out suggests being thrown about, so the letters are scattered and reset

explanation.surface: A fake delegation is thrown out, causing a melodramatic fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means overdoing pathos, laying it on thick about suffering.
